hero_framing:
**$7.3M invoiced** in the trailing twelve months through June 29, 2026 — 29,052 invoice lines. The growth story is new lines, not a returning-dealer comparison: this book is **1,004** first-year accounts, one year of invoices deep.

**What stands out:**
1. **ROMA cleared $596K across 150 dealers in year one.** SLIM ($371K, 31 dealers), PILSON ($364K, 120 dealers), and MODPLUS ($281K, 111 dealers) all posted real first-year volume.
2. **$614K of trailing-twelve-month invoices carry no bill-to number.** They group as one nameless block, so those dollars cannot be assigned to a dealer, a rep, or a territory. That is a record-keeping gap to close, not an account to call.
3. **Every booked dollar lands in one unmapped channel.** The channel field is carrying no signal at all, so nothing in this report can yet separate showroom from project from online.
talking_points: Cx Connect is down 55% on a $30K book and 103 days dark. Is the buyer relationship intact, or has something structurally changed.
coaching_narratives: Ksa Lighting Inc. carries one slipping account: Cx Connect, a $30K book down 55% with 103 days of silence. Small dollars, unambiguous slope — one call to find out whether the line is still on the floor.

growth_connective.layer_1: Same-dealer year-over-year is not available — this is one year of invoices, 1,004 first-year accounts, not a missing comparison from catalog-app orders. The cadence split (frequent / occasional / one-time) is the durability read until a second invoiced year exists.
growth_connective.layer_2: ROMA did $596K across 150 dealers in its first year — 8.1% of invoiced LTM on a new line, 9 SKUs. That is 150 separate dealers, not a promotional spike on a handful of doors.
growth_connective.layer_3: Brand Jump LLC invoiced $2.4M — 33% of the business — across 20 dealers. Lumen Resource ($515K, 41 dealers) and Performance Lighting Systems ($358K, 75 dealers) are next. No prior-year comparison is available for any of those books; this is year one of the record.

outreach_framing: One account clears the bar this week: a real decline, not a soft patch. A short list on a $7.3M book is the good version of this section — the decay is not broad-based.
